$comment: FALSIFICATION EXERCISE. Chosen to break the model, not to confirm it.
A notice under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 is the hardest case
so far, because almost nothing about its legal effect is in the words. It must be given
within thirty days of receipt of the bank's return memo; the cause of action arises only
on failure to pay within fifteen days of ITS receipt; and the complaint must follow
within a month of that. A flawlessly drafted notice served on day thirty-one is worth
The two timing requirements below are deliberately authored as CONTENT to see whether
the model reports them green. It does. That is the finding.

requirements.statement: The notice demands payment of the cheque amount in terms capable of being complied with.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and there is no demand, and proviso (b) to section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 is not satisfied however clearly the dishonour is described.

requirements.statement: The cheque, its dishonour and the bank's reason are particularised.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the drawer cannot identify which instrument is complained of, and the notice fails for uncertainty.

requirements.statement: The debt or liability the cheque was issued to discharge is stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and section 138 does not apply at all: it reaches only a cheque drawn for the discharge of a legally enforceable debt or other liability.

requirements.statement: The fifteen-day period for payment is stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the drawer is not told the period proviso (c) gives him, and the notice may be read as demanding immediate payment.

requirements.statement: The consequence of non-payment is stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the notice reads as a request rather than a statutory demand.

requirements.statement: The notice is given within thirty days of receipt of the bank's return memo.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and there is no offence to complain of: proviso (b) to section 138 makes the thirty-day window a condition of the cause of action, and it cannot be extended by anything the notice says.
requirements.window: Thirty days from receipt of the bank's return memo.
requirements.depends_on_event: the drawer's receipt of the bank's memo returning the cheque unpaid

requirements.statement: A complaint is filed within one month of the cause of action arising.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and section 142(1)(b) bars the court from taking cognizance, whatever the merits.
requirements.window: One month from the cause of action, which arises fifteen days after the drawer receives this notice.
requirements.depends_on_event: the expiry of the fifteen-day payment period, itself running from service of this notice
requirements.$note: Deliberately left with no computable_from: the complaint has not been filed and the system cannot know when it will be. UNVERIFIABLE is the honest answer.
